signature.name: Royal Exhibition Building
signature.detail: A UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the world's oldest surviving exhibition halls, it is the grand centrepiece of Carlton Gardens. Visit on a weekday morning for quieter gardens, and check ahead whether interior tours are running since access is often limited to guided visits.

signature.name: Flinders Street Station
signature.detail: The city's most photographed facade, a yellow Edwardian landmark sitting right on the Yarra at the main rail hub. It is free to admire from the corner of Swanston and Flinders Streets; come at dusk when the clocks and dome light up.

signature.name: Shrine of Remembrance
signature.detail: Victoria's solemn war memorial, with a crypt, gallery and a rooftop balcony giving sweeping views over the city. Entry is free; it is a short walk from the Royal Botanic Gardens and best visited in the cooler morning hours.

signature.name: Federation Square
signature.detail: The city's central urban hub, home to major museums and galleries and a natural meeting point by the river. Drop by for the architecture and events, then walk across to the Yarra for the riverside promenade.

signature.name: National Gallery of Victoria
signature.detail: Australia's oldest and most visited public gallery, with a strong international and Australian collection and a famous stained-glass ceiling. General entry is free; allow a few hours and check opening days before you go.

signature.name: Queen Victoria Market
signature.detail: A sprawling historic market for produce, deli goods and souvenirs, and a Melbourne institution. Go early in the morning for the freshest food and fewer crowds; it is a short tram ride from the central grid.

signature.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
signature.detail: One of the world's great sports stadiums and the spiritual home of Australian cricket and football. Book a stadium tour or catch a match; the surrounding parkland is an easy walk from the city.

signature.name: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria
signature.detail: Lush, free gardens along the river with lakes, lawns and themed plant collections. Enter from the Shrine side and bring water and sun protection; it is ideal for a relaxed half-day.

signature.name: Eureka Tower
signature.detail: A soaring skyscraper whose Skydeck offers the best high views over the city and bay. Go near sunset for day-to-night views, and book tickets online to skip queues.

signature.name: St Kilda Beach
signature.detail: The city's classic seaside escape, with a pier, promenade and nearby penguin viewing at dusk. Take a tram from the centre and allow time to wander the foreshore.

transport: Tram or train about $3-5 a ride; day passes good value
